buys.reasoning: Micron's Q3 FY2026 print was the most decisive earnings beat of the AI supercycle: revenue $41.5B (+346% YoY, vs $34.7B consensus), EPS $25.04 (vs $20.20, +24% beat), gross margin 84.6% (record), net income $28.2B. Q4 guidance of $50B revenue with 86% margins came in $6.4B above expectations — a 14.7% guide-beat before the quarter started. HBM4 is in high-volume production for the lead customer (Nvidia Vera Rubin) with bandwidth above 2.8 TB/s and 20% better power efficiency vs HBM3E; $1B+ in HBM4 revenue already shipped this quarter. Nvidia certified Micron (alongside Samsung and SK Hynix) for Vera Rubin HBM4 supply, confirming a structural multi-year revenue floor. 41% Strong Buy / 55% Buy analyst consensus (96% Buy). BofA target $1,500 (+32% from ~$1,133); Phillip Securities raised to $1,870; average 12m target ~$1,410. Post-ATH pullback from $1,255 to ~$1,133 (-9.7%) is exactly the 'buy the dip after strong earnings' setup flagged in last week's watchlist. The June 22 plan explicitly identified MU post-earnings as top candidate if blackout lifted. RSI was 34.7 in stale bars (approaching oversold); actual RSI likely similar given pullback from ATH. Forward P/E below 12x on $50B quarterly run-rate is extremely attractive for a structural HBM leader.

hold_reasoning.AMAT: Portfolio's defining winner at +58% from $411.45 entry (current ~$650, 52-week high $669.22 set June 25). Applied Materials Master Class June 25 unveiled 6 new AI chipmaking systems targeting DRAM production and AI chip advanced packaging — direct address of the 'memory wall' constraining AI compute. This drove a 13.42% single-day surge to ATH $669.22 intraday. Immediate analyst target upgrades: Jefferies $770, B. Riley $790, Wells Fargo $740, BofA $720 (all Buy/Overweight). Pre-market June 29: +3.8% to $650.52 recovering from June 26 -4.36% pullback. AI semiconductor equipment supercycle is a multi-year secular theme; AMAT's equipment is essential to DRAM scaling and HBM4 production (directly correlated to MU's boom). Next earnings August 13 — no near-term event risk. Updated trailing stop: $617 (5% below ~$650, up from prior $586 trailing stop).
hold_reasoning.LLY: Healthcare anchor with structural GLP-1 dominance. Up +24% from $992.17 entry to $1,229.77 (June 29 close). Two major catalysts this week: (1) European regulators backed Jaypirca (Pirtobrutinib) for cancer treatment June 26, lifting stock +6.15%; (2) Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Program launches July 1 — eligible Medicare Part D patients access Zepbound and Foundayo at $50/month; Lilly estimates ~20 million Medicare patients may meet clinical criteria — an enormous new recurring revenue channel. Leerink raised target to $1,232 June 25. Healthcare sector is defensively positioned relative to semiconductor volatility. LLY is low-rate-sensitivity vs NVDA/AMD. Stop $942 (5% below $992.17 entry, unchanged — wide buffer at +24% gain). Next earnings in late July — monitor for Mounjaro Q2 results.
